paragraphs: Gray Decision Intelligence sells analytics software that colleges and universities use to weigh their academic programs. The product is the Program Evaluation System, which the company calls the only complete one for higher education. It is meant to help institutions make decisions that increase revenue, reduce cost and save time.

One part of the system tracks revenue, cost and margin by college, department, program and course. Another reports student demand, competition, wages, skills and jobs across more than 1,500 academic programs and six award levels. Dashboards give a snapshot of program indicators for budget allocation and management. Written reports are generated automatically, distilling more than 50 metrics into short summaries for over 1,500 IPEDS programs. A facilitated workshop puts course data in front of faculty and administrators, who use their own judgment to find efficiencies in the courses and sections offered.

Case studies describe Utah Valley University evaluating program economics down to the course level. Another describes Tiffin University streamlining its review process and reaching 25 percent year-over-year growth in eight programs. A third credits the software with helping Jessup University avoid launching low-demand programs.

quote.text: My message to other universities is that if you are committed to having a process of ongoing program evaluation based on internal and external data analysis, you need Gray PES.
